findings.finding: Insights: Final scores are all 0‑2²⁰‑1 binary numbers; ordering = permutation of runners to these numbers. Pairings within equal‑score groups are arbitrary matchings, winners (faster) get the next bit. N = product over all groups of (size‑1)!! (number of perfect matchings). For each round i, groups of size 2^{20-i} appear 2^{i-1} times, giving factor ((2^{20-i})! / (2^{20-i-1}!·2^{20-i-1}!))? Actually number of matchings = (2^{20-i})!/(2^{(20-i-1)}!·2^{(20-i-1)}!·2^{20-i-1}!). Compute v₂,v₅ of N via Legendre sums; k = min(v₂,v₅); output k mod 10⁵. (Key pitfall: correct matching count formula).

Insights: Final scores are 20‑bit binary strings (win = 1). Pairings only allow matches between identical prefixes, so any binary tree consistent with speed order is possible. Count linear extensions of the poset where runner a < b iff a beats b in some round. This equals product of factorials of group sizes at each score level. Compute v₂,v₅ of N via Legendre sums; k = min(v₂,v₅) mod 10⁵. Watch for ties (identical scores) and ensure all matchings counted.

Insights: Scores = 20‑bit win‑loss strings; round i pairs equal prefixes. Within any equal‑score group of size 2n, possible winner sets are exactly Catalan Cₙ (Dyck condition). Thus each round splits groups recursively, giving a binary tree of Catalan choices. The final ranking depends only on which players end in each leaf (full 20‑bit string). Number of achievable total orders N = product over all groups of (size)! where sizes are leaf‑group multiplicities obtainable via Catalan splits. Compute v₂(N), v₅(N) via factorial exponents and Catalan counts; k = min(v₂,v₅). Beware: treat ties (identical scores) as permutable; ensure all Catalan possibilities counted. Use recursion to sum factorial exponents across all possible leaf‑size distributions.

Insights: After 20 rounds each runner gets a unique 20‑bit win/loss string; scores are distinct. The tournament builds a full binary tree where each internal node pairs two equal‑score groups; the faster must be on the “win” side. Thus any leaf labeling (bijection runner↔binary string) is realizable iff for every node the runner assigned to the win child is faster than the one assigned to the lose child. This is exactly the set of linear extensions of the poset defined by the tree’s parent‑child “win > lose” relations. Count = number of permutations respecting these 2²⁰⁻¹ pairwise constraints. Compute N = (2^{20})! / ∏_{node} (size_of_subtree). Then find k = ν_{10}(N) and output k mod 10⁵. Pitfalls: ensure each node’s subtree size = 2^{depth}; product = ∏_{i=0}^{19} (2^{i})^{2^{20-i}}. Compute ν₂, ν₅ via Legendre sums.

Insights: Scores = 20‑bit win/loss strings; ranking = binary order. At each node (players with same prefix) winners must be a set W of size half that can be matched to distinct slower losers L ⇒ no winner is slower than any loser. Thus W must be the top half of the group’s speeds. Hence the tournament forces a deterministic partition: at every round the faster half get a 1, slower half a 0. Consequently each player’s final binary string is exactly the binary representation of its rank among the 2²⁰ speeds (most‑significant bit = top‑half split, etc.). Therefore the final ordering is uniquely determined – only one ordering possible, N=1, so k=0, answer 0.

Insights: After each round every equal‑score group of size 2^{m} splits into two halves (winners/losers). Any half can be winners because we can pair each winner with a slower loser (Hall’s condition always holds). Thus each round independently chooses, for every group, which 2^{m‑1} become winners. Consequently the final binary win‑vector for each runner can be any 20‑bit string, giving a bijection between runners and binary numbers. Hence every permutation of the 2^{20} runners is attainable as the final ranking. So N = (2^{20})! . The exponent k of 10 dividing N is v₁₀((2^{20})!) = ⌊2^{20}/5⌋+⌊2^{20}/25⌋+… = 209715. Finally, k mod 10⁵ = 209715.

Insights: After 20 rounds each runner gets a unique 20‑bit score, so final ranking = permutation of runners onto the 2²⁰ leaves. At each node of size 2^m the winners (right child) must be a “ballot” set → Catalan C_{2^{m‑1}} possibilities. Choices at different nodes are independent. Hence  

\(N=\displaystyle\prod_{m=1}^{20}\Big(C_{2^{m-1}}\Big)^{2^{20-m}}\)  

(where each Catalan appears for every node at that depth). Compute v₂(N) and v₅(N) from this product, then k=min(v₂,v₅) mod 10⁵. Pitfall: ignore pairings count; only winner‑set choices matter. Use Legendre’s formula for 2‑ and 5‑adic valuations of binomial coefficients.

Insights: Final scores are 20‑bit binary; each round splits a block of 2^r players into winners/losers of size 2^{r‑1}. A split is possible iff the winner set satisfies the ballot (Dyck) condition → count = Catalan_{2^{r‑1}}.  

Thus total orderings  

\(N=\prod_{r=2}^{20} \big(C_{2^{\,r-1}}\big)^{2^{20-r}}\)  

where \(C_n=\frac1{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}\).  

Compute N’s 10‑adic valuation: \(k=v_{10}(N)=\sum_{r=2}^{20}2^{20-r}\,v_{10}(C_{2^{r-1}})\).  

Use Legendre: \(v_p(C_n)=v_p((2n)!)-2v_p(n!)-v_p(n+1)\).  

Sum contributions for p=2,5; obtain \(k\).  

Finally output \(k\bmod 10^5\).   (Avoid overflow; use big integers or modular arithmetic.)

Insights: Each round splits a group of 2m runners into “right” (winners) and “left” (losers). A split is possible iff the sequence of rights/lefts never has more lefts than rights in any prefix → Catalan Cₘ choices.  

Thus total orderings  
\(N=\prod_{depth\;r=0}^{19} C_{2^{19-r}}^{\,2^{r}}=\prod_{j=0}^{19}C_{2^{j}}^{\,2^{19-j}}\).  

Valuations: \(v_2(C_{2^{j}})=1\) for j≥1, \(v_5(C_{2^{j}})\) computed via Legendre.  

\(v_2(N)=\sum_{j=1}^{19}2^{19-j}=2^{19}-1=524287\).  

\(v_5(N)=\sum_{j=0}^{19}2^{19-j}v_5(C_{2^{j}})=121818\).  

\(k=\min(v_2,v_5)=121818\).  

Answer: \(k\bmod10^{5}=21818\).  

Pitfalls: Confusing “winners set” with “top half”; need Catalan condition, not all‑faster. Use product over all internal nodes, not just round matchings.

Insights: Each round splits every equal‑score group (size 2n) into winners/losers; feasible winner sets are exactly the Catalan number Cₙ (Dyck condition on speed order). Groups are independent.  

Result:  
N = ∏_{i=1}^{20} (C_{2^{20‑i}})^{2^{i‑1}}.  

Compute v₂(N), v₅(N) via vₚ(Cₙ)=vₚ( (2n)! )‑vₚ(n! )‑vₚ((n+1)! ). Sum over i with multiplicities 2^{i‑1}.

Insights: Final scores are unique 20‑bit strings; ranking = binary order. Pairings each round give a perfect matching within each equal‑score bucket, i.e. a binary‑tree of comparisons. The tournament yields a poset where each internal node forces the “winner” element to be larger than the “loser”. Counting N = number of linear extensions of this poset (all possible total orders realizable by some choice of matchings). Pitfalls: assume scores distinct (true – groups halve each round). Must treat matchings as arbitrary, not fixed. Compute N via DP on tree: for a node with left/right sub‑sets of size m, number of extensions = C(2m, m)·L·R (choose interleaving of left/right orders). Recursively multiply; final N = ∏_{i=1}^{20} (C(2^{i},2^{i-1}) )^{2^{20-i}}. Then k = v_{10}(N) = Σ v_{10}(C(2^{i},2^{i-1}))·2^{20-i}. Compute k mod 10^5.

Insights: After 20 rounds each player gets a unique 20‑bit score; ranking = permutation of players. A valid permutation ⇔ for every node of the binary split tree (size 2^t) the left/right split of its ordered players is a Dyck word (half 0/1, never more 1’s than 0’s).  

Count: For a group of size 2n the number of splits = Catalanₙ. Recurrence g(2⁰)=1, g(2ⁿ)=Catalan_{2^{n‑1}}·g(2^{n‑1})². Hence  

\(N=\prod_{t=0}^{19} C_{2^{t}}^{\,2^{19-t}}\) where \(C_m\) is Catalan.  

Prime valuations: \(v_2(C_{2^{t}})=0\) for t=0, =1 otherwise; \(v_5(C_{2^{t}})\) for t=0…19 are  
0,0,0,1,1,0,2,1,0,1,1,3,3,4,0,2,3,5,4,6.  

Thus  

\(v_2(N)=\sum_{t=1}^{19}2^{19-t}=2^{19}-1=524287\)  

\(v_5(N)=\sum_{t=0}^{19}2^{19-t}·v_5(C_{2^{t}})=121818\).  

\(k=\min(v_2,v_5)=121818\).  

Answer: \(k\bmod10^{5}=21818\).  

Pitfalls: assume scores distinct (they are, groups halve each round); ensure Dyck condition is both necessary and sufficient for realizability.
